chunks: He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fazari al-Bazzaz narrated from a group of the Shia, including Ali ibn Bilal, Ahmad ibn Hilal, Muhammad ibn Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, and al-Hasan ibn Ayyub ibn Nuh, in a famous lengthy report.

They all said: We gathered before Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them) to ask him about the Hujjah (Proof/Imam) after him. There were forty men in his gathering. Uthman ibn Saeed ibn Amr al-Amari rose to him and said to him: 'O son of Allah's Messenger, I wish to ask you about a matter of which you have more knowledge than I.' He said to him: 'Sit down, O Uthman.' He rose angrily to leave, so he said: 'Let no one leave.' None of us left until an hour had passed. The Imam called out to Uthman, so he stood on his feet and said: 'Shall I inform you why you came?' They said: 'Yes, O son of Allah's Messenger.' He said: 'You came to ask me about the Hujjah after me.' They said: 'Yes.' Then a boy appeared, as if he were a drop of moonlight, the most similar of people to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said: 'This is your Imam after me and my caliph over you. Obey him and do not disperse after me, lest you perish in your religion. Indeed, you will not see him after this day of yours until his age is completed. So accept from Uthman what he says, and submit to his command, and accept his word, for he is the caliph of your Imam and the affair is in his hands...' In a lengthy hadith.

key_terms.أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ: Abu Muhammad, referring to Imam al-Hasan al-'Askari (a.s.)
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: The Proof (of God), a title for the Imam
key_terms.عُثْمَانُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ: Uthman ibn Saeed, the first deputy of the Imam during the Minor Occultation

ai.seo_question: Who did Imam al-Askari designate as his deputy during the occultation?
ai.summary: This pivotal hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* records the final public designation of the Twelfth Imam, al-Hassan al-Muntazar, by his father, Imam al-Hasan al-'Askari, before the onset of the Minor Exaltation. It highlights the crucial role of Uthman ibn Saeed al-Amri as the first deputy (al-Khalif al-Awwal), establishing the precedent for the Imam's hidden authority being mediated through his appointed representatives during the period when the Imam would not be directly seen by the general public.
